newsitem.title: FINLAND: Weaker forestries, Motorola warning hit Helsinki.
newsitem.headline: Weaker forestries, Motorola warning hit Helsinki.

text.p: Finnish shares ended a nervous bourse session slightly lower prompted by a sharp fall in forestries and a slide in telecoms major Nokia, brokers said.

Nokia closed official trade down four markka at 187.00, but largely rebounded from an initial shock after U.S. rival Motorola said its third-quarter earnings would fall short of the previous period's result.

"It is too early to say whether Motorola's earnings warning was only bad news for Nokia," one broker said. "But in the short term, the Motorola warning is likely to depress the whole technology sector," he added.
Forestries tracked Swedish paper stocks lower, taking the sub-index down 2.12 percent.
"There were clear selling pressures in forestries today, and it seemed to be a Nordic phenomenon," one broker said.
Forestry giant UPM-Kymmene closed down two markka at 99.00, in low volume, and Enso shed 0.80 markka to 36.50.
